cards.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Resolving multiple exact IDs, canonical titles, registered aliases, and authority-backed identity corrections in one input-ordered batch.

Preserving ambiguous and unresolved references as explicit outcomes instead of dropping or guessing them.
not_for: Fuzzy, semantic, natural-language, web, or cross-repository identity search.
Changing identities, repairing source data, or writing results into the repository.
Establishing scientific truth, proof, external validity, or evidence quality.

counterindicated_when: The task requires fresh external sources, fuzzy matching, or resolution beyond the checked-out repository snapshot.

estimated_cost.basis: The resolver rebuilds exact lookup indexes for each reference; no comparable batch latency or memory benchmark has been established.

alternatives.reason: The Current operation exposes the single-reference resolver contract; this experimental CLI adds ordered multi-reference input and a batch receipt while reusing that resolver algorithm.

cards.fallback: For one reference, use the existing foundation.resolve_current_asset operation or ignition/tools/foundation/resolve_current_canonical_asset.py --reference; if this batch tool is unavailable, process references individually and preserve each unresolved or ambiguous status.

negative_controls: Unknown, historical-path, and near-match references remain explicitly unresolved in input order.
Malformed batches, path traversal, and symlinked authorities fail closed without partial stdout output.
Running the CLI creates or changes no repository files.

router_conditions: Include only through an explicit experimental-tool allowlist for exact multi-reference repository identity resolution.
The route proposal does not execute the tool; the caller must separately authorize and supply the specific batch input.
Do not select when fuzzy matching, external freshness, scientific judgment, or automatic identity repair is required.
cards.claim_ceiling: Repository-snapshot canonical identity and migration resolution only; ambiguous and unresolved rows remain explicit; no fuzzy identity, truth, proof, evidence upgrade, or external validity is inferred.

cards.description: Run one explicitly supplied, single-output pure symbolic FunctionSpec through Function OS N1-N7 with bounded expression size, arithmetic intermediates, and numeric input magnitude.
cards.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Run one declared deterministic symbolic function with one output and 1 to 16 explicitly supplied numeric or boolean inputs.
Inspect the N1-N7 execution status, in-memory artifact integrity report, trace, and N7 internal consistency checks for a bounded specification.
not_for: Executing untrusted or malicious code, acting as an isolated security sandbox, or processing arbitrary Python expressions.
Scientific adjudication, proof, empirical validation, external truth claims, or recognition that a function models reality.
Stateful or I/O effects, multiple outputs, exponentiation, calls, attributes, N8 routing, N9 registry writes, or persisted artifacts.
only_if: Python 3.10 or newer is available and the checked-out Function OS v0.2 source and wrapper are intact.
The caller supplies a single symbolic FunctionSpec with exactly one output, exactly pure effects, 1 to 16 declared inputs, and one output equality postcondition.

The UTF-8 JSON request is at most 16 KiB; expressions are at most 512 characters, 64 AST nodes, and depth 16; numeric inputs/constants are at most 10^12 in magnitude and arithmetic intermediates/results at most 10^100.
counterindicated_when: Inputs or expressions are adversarial and require operating-system isolation or a security boundary.
The specification needs exponentiation, calls, attributes, strings, collections, multiple outputs, non-pure effects, or values beyond the declared bounds.
The task requires persistence, registry admission, source-backed evidence, scientific truth, proof, or external validation.
accepted_input_types: UTF-8 JSON stdin object containing exactly one bounded FunctionSpec object and one exact input-value object
output_types: N1-N7 execution status and single declared output when successful
in-memory artifact integrity report, execution trace, and N7 internal consistency result
side_effects: Writes the bounded JSON result to stdout; execution artifacts and traces remain in process memory and N9 is not invoked.
The wrapper disables Python bytecode writes before loading Function OS modules.
runtime_dependencies: Python >=3.10 standard library; no third-party runtime packages

estimated_cost.basis: Execution is local and bounded by request and AST limits, but no latency or memory benchmark has been established.

cards.fallback: Use the checked-in Function OS N1-N7 tests on Python 3.10 or newer and inspect the exact specification and expected outputs manually; do not substitute eval, a general Python runner, or a scientific-validity claim.

negative_controls: Calls, attributes, exponentiation, multiple outputs, non-pure effects, oversized inputs, and oversized intermediate arithmetic are rejected.
Duplicate JSON keys and requests over 16 KiB return nonzero with no partial stdout; division by zero is rejected by the bounded arithmetic preflight.
Precondition failure is preserved; N9 registry writes are never invoked; a passing N7 status is explicitly limited to internal consistency.

router_conditions: Include only through an explicit experimental-tool allowlist when the task supplies a bounded pure symbolic FunctionSpec and asks for its local N1-N7 execution report.
A route proposal never runs the function; the caller separately supplies the complete FunctionSpec and inputs to the CLI.
Never select for arbitrary code, scientific proof, truth, registry admission, or effectful execution.
cards.claim_ceiling: A bounded local execution report for one pure symbolic FunctionSpec through Function OS N1-N7, with internal artifact/trace consistency checks only; it does not establish specification truth, empirical or scientific correctness, proof, external validation, security isolation, registry admission, or publication status.

cards.description: Read the raw Comments/Corrections relations recorded for exact PubMed PMIDs from the fixed NCBI EFetch endpoint.
cards.license: Wrapper BUSL-1.1; NCBI E-utilities usage terms apply, and no license for underlying PubMed record data is asserted. API documentation: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25499/.
cards.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Reading raw PubMed Comments/Corrections RefType, citation text, and linked PMID fields for one or more already-known PubMed records.
Recording whether a specific PubMed response contains relation rows without interpreting the relation as a full scientific or editorial adjudication.
Reviewing a known PubMed record after a caller has obtained its PMID directly or through a separately selected identifier resolver.
not_for: Retrieving, displaying, or reviewing article titles, abstracts, full text, or arbitrary publisher content; the upstream XML may contain an abstract but this wrapper discards it.
Proving that a paper is or is not retracted, corrected, valid, authentic, or scientifically supported.
Treating an empty or missing Comments/Corrections list as evidence that no update exists.
Searching for PMIDs from arbitrary text or changing a repository research record.
only_if: The caller supplies one to ten exact numeric PubMed IDs and explicitly permits sending those identifiers to NCBI for this invocation.
The caller invokes the CLI with --allow-public-network.
The exact host eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov is permitted by the actual invocation environment; a route proposal alone is not authority.
The caller understands that only the update links present in the returned record are reported.
counterindicated_when: The PMID or its presence in task context is confidential or must not be sent to a public service.
Network access is unavailable, disallowed, or not explicitly approved for this invocation.
The task requires complete retraction status, article-content review, source-authenticity review, or scientific assessment.
accepted_input_types: JSON stdin object with one to ten unique numeric PubMed IDs (PMIDs)
output_types: input-ordered PubMed comments/corrections relation rows with raw RefType, related PMID, and reference source
per-response SHA-256 and explicit HTTP or network outcome summary
side_effects: When explicitly invoked with --allow-public-network, sends at most ten HTTPS GET requests to https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi with the supplied PMID and fixed PubMed/XML/tool parameters.

The upstream XML response may contain a full PubMed record including an abstract; the wrapper parses only the exact PMID and CommentsCorrectionsList, discards the rest, emits no abstract/title, writes only JSON to stdout, and creates or modifies no repository files.

Uses no redirects, secrets, API key, billing, retry, or arbitrary URL; applies a five-second socket timeout, seven-second response-body budget with bounded 8 KiB reads, 256 KiB response cap, and 0.34-second serial inter-request delay.

estimated_cost.basis: No comparable latency, bandwidth, service-availability, or compute-cost profile has been measured; the wrapper allows at most ten serial bounded PubMed XML requests.

alternatives.reason: The identifier resolver maps DOI values to returned PMID/PMCID values; this tool requires an exact PMID and reads only the record's raw comments/corrections relations.

cards.fallback: If live network use is not approved or fails, preserve NOT_RUN or the acquisition failure and open the official PubMed record manually only when the caller separately authorizes that lookup; never infer no update from an empty/unavailable response.

negative_controls: Missing --allow-public-network makes no request and emits no result.
Reject malformed, duplicate, nonnumeric, URL-like, and over-limit PMIDs before network access.
Only eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov is contacted; redirects, non-XML, oversized responses, HTTP errors, timeout, malformed XML, entity declarations, and mismatched PMID records remain explicit outcomes.
Return raw relation fields without article titles/abstracts; empty relation lists remain limited observations and no repository files are written.

router_conditions: Remain excluded unless the candidate ID is explicitly allowlisted and the typed route profile explicitly lists eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov in allowed_network_hosts.
A route proposal has execution_authorized=false and does not validate the caller authority behind that host list.
Every actual CLI invocation separately requires --allow-public-network and a task-specific decision to transmit the supplied PMID values.
cards.claim_ceiling: Raw PubMed Comments/Corrections fields for exact records at retrieval time only; the response may omit relationships that exist elsewhere or have not been added, so no completeness, retraction-status, content, authenticity, scientific-validity, or absence claim is established.

good_for: Mapping caller-supplied DOI identifiers to PubMed PMID and PMC PMCID values when those identifiers are returned by NCBI's ID Converter.
Retaining per-DOI source response hashes, HTTP outcomes, and explicit no-match results.
Adding an NCBI/PMC identifier lookup alongside a separately requested Crossref DOI metadata comparison.
not_for: Retrieving article full text, abstracts, publisher pages, or arbitrary URLs.
Establishing that a paper is authentic, scientifically correct, retracted, or supports a claim.
Treating a missing PMID or PMCID as proof that a DOI or article does not exist.
Adding or correcting repository records or registering scientific sources.
only_if: The caller provides one to ten unique bare DOI identifiers and explicitly permits sending those DOI identifiers to the public API for this invocation.
The caller invokes the CLI with --allow-public-network.
The exact fixed host pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov is allowed by the actual invocation environment; route context alone is not authority.
The PMC ID Converter endpoint is reachable and returns a supported JSON response.
counterindicated_when: A DOI or its presence in task context is confidential or must not be sent to a public service.
Network access is unavailable, disallowed, or not explicitly approved for this invocation.
The task requires article-content review, source-authenticity review, retraction adjudication, or scientific assessment.
accepted_input_types: JSON stdin object with one to ten unique bare DOI identifiers
output_types: per-response SHA-256 and explicit HTTP or network outcome summary
side_effects: When explicitly invoked with --allow-public-network, sends at most ten HTTPS GET requests to the fixed pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/tools/idconv/api/v1/articles/ endpoint; only the DOI identifier and response-format parameter are sent.
Uses no redirects, secrets, API key, billing, or arbitrary URL. Returns a compact JSON receipt on stdout and validation errors on stderr; does not create or modify repository files.

Applies a five-second socket timeout, seven-second response-body budget checked between and after bounded 8 KiB reads, a 128 KiB response cap, and a serial 0.34-second inter-request delay; no retries are performed.

estimated_cost.basis: No comparable latency, bandwidth, service-availability, or compute-cost profile has been measured; the wrapper has a maximum of ten serial fixed-host lookups and bounded response handling.

alternatives.reason: Crossref compares caller-supplied DOI title/year expectations with Crossref metadata; this tool maps DOI identifiers to NCBI PMID/PMCID values and does not verify title or year.

cards.fallback: If live network use is not approved or fails, preserve the explicit NOT_RUN or acquisition failure and use the official PubMed/PMC interface manually only when the caller separately authorizes that lookup; never infer an absent record from an unavailable response.

negative_controls: Missing --allow-public-network makes no request and emits no result.
Reject URLs, malformed or duplicate DOI identifiers, duplicate JSON keys, and batches above ten before network access.
Only pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov is contacted; redirects, non-JSON, oversized responses, HTTP errors, timeout, malformed JSON, mismatched records, and invalid identifiers remain explicit outcomes.
A no-match response yields no invented PMID/PMCID; no repository files are written.

router_conditions: Remain excluded unless the candidate ID is explicitly allowlisted and the typed route profile explicitly lists pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov in allowed_network_hosts.
A route proposal has execution_authorized=false and does not validate the caller authority behind that host list.
Every actual CLI invocation separately requires --allow-public-network and a task-specific decision to transmit the supplied DOI identifiers.
cards.claim_ceiling: DOI-to-PMID/PMCID identifier lookup from the live PMC ID Converter response only; response hashes bind received bytes, not source authenticity, article content, bibliographic accuracy, scientific truth, retraction status, or complete PubMed/PMC coverage.

cards.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.

Get a compact check/failure count and SHA-256 digest for the entire fixed Evidence Program input tree.
not_for: Running Crossref, OpenAlex, model, browser, search, or other network queries; the source-acquisition runner is a separate tool with different permissions.
Authenticating source origins, proving every file was committed as claimed, verifying scientific content, deciding truth, or recording independent/human acceptance.
Editing manifests, registrations, run records, thresholds, or the evidence-program tree.
only_if: The caller wants to validate the fixed `ignition/evidence-program/` snapshot in the currently checked-out Formal repository.
Python >=3.9 and the local Git CLI are available; Git is used only for repository-root discovery and preregistration ancestor checks.
The caller understands that the result validates recorded structure and consistency only, and that checkout-level Git metadata is read-only input.
counterindicated_when: The task asks to fetch or refresh any evidence source; use a separately authorized acquisition workflow with network and output-path controls.
The task requires scientific adjudication, primary-source support review, authorship/authenticity proof, or epistemic acceptance.
The tool router must authorize an exact Git metadata read path; the current route planner cannot represent the containing checkout's `.git` metadata and will fail closed.
accepted_input_types: fixed checked-out ignition/evidence-program snapshot plus containing checkout Git metadata for read-only ancestry checks
output_types: compact validator status, check count, failure count, and bounded failure details
SHA-256 digest and file count for the complete checked-out Evidence Program tree
validator source SHA-256 and local Git root identity

read_paths: containing checkout Git metadata (read-only; `git rev-parse` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` only)

side_effects: Writes one compact JSON summary to stdout; no repository files are created or changed.
Runs the validator and fixed-argument local Git read commands as child processes; never invokes a shell or a remote Git operation.
runtime_dependencies: Python >=3.9 standard library and local Git CLI; no third-party runtime packages

estimated_cost.basis: The fixed tree has 31 files and 499 observed checks in the current run, but no calibrated latency or memory profile has been established.

alternatives.reason: The upstream validator exposes a configurable root and a verbose per-check log; this wrapper fixes the repository root and summarizes the same validator run.

cards.fallback: Run the upstream validator directly with `--root ignition/evidence-program` when full per-check output is needed; if local Git ancestry cannot be read, report validation unavailable rather than inferring an ordering pass.

negative_controls: A modified schema, missing provenance field, changed threshold, leaked metric, or failed recorded preregistration ordering remains a validator failure and returns a nonzero status.
The wrapper has no caller-controlled root, output path, network option, or mutation operation; invalid checkout identity fails closed.
The adaptive route planner must reject the candidate because the declared local Git metadata read is outside its ignition/ path authority.

router_conditions: Direct CLI invocation only after an explicit task request; the current typed route planner is expected to reject the Git metadata path as unavailable or unsafe.
Do not remove the Git metadata dependency to make routing pass; preregistration ancestry is one of the validator's declared checks.
Never use the result as evidence of scientific truth, source authenticity, acceptance, or publication readiness.
cards.claim_ceiling: The fixed checked-out Evidence Program tree passed or failed this repository validator's schema and recorded-consistency checks, with local Git metadata read-only; no source authenticity, committed-file binding, scientific truth, independent review, acceptance, or publication is established.

cards.description: Compare up to ten caller-supplied DOI title/year expectations against live Crossref bibliographic metadata using bounded fixed-host HTTPS GET requests.
cards.license: Wrapper BUSL-1.1; Crossref bibliographic metadata reuse basis documented at https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/.
cards.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; Task 103 Crossref pilot supplies reused normalization helpers, not Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Comparing caller-supplied expected DOI title and year with the live Crossref metadata record.
Retaining per-record HTTP outcome, response SHA-256, observed fields, and explicit mismatch or network-failure status.
Checking public bibliographic metadata for a bounded batch without retrieving article content.
not_for: Retrieving article full text, abstracts, publisher pages, or arbitrary URLs.
Establishing that a paper is authentic, scientifically correct, or supports a claim.
Treating missing or stale Crossref fields as proof that a source does not exist.
Adding or correcting records in a repository registry.
only_if: The caller has explicitly approved transmission of the DOI identifiers in this invocation and passes --allow-public-network.
A route proposal may include this candidate only when allowed_network_hosts explicitly contains api.crossref.org; the proposal is not a permission grant.
The request contains one to ten unique bare DOI identifiers with caller-supplied expected title and year.
The public Crossref REST API is reachable from the declared environment.
counterindicated_when: The DOI or associated task context is confidential or must not be sent to a public service.
Network access is unavailable, disallowed, or not explicitly approved for this invocation.
The task requires article-content review, source authenticity, current retraction adjudication, or scientific assessment.
accepted_input_types: UTF-8 JSON stdin object with one to ten unique DOI, expected-title, expected-year records
output_types: per-response SHA-256 and explicit HTTP or network outcome summary
side_effects: When explicitly invoked with --allow-public-network, sends at most ten HTTPS GET requests to api.crossref.org with DOI identifiers only; no user title, source_id, credential, or arbitrary URL is transmitted.
Writes the JSON result to stdout and validation errors to stderr; does not create or modify repository files.

Follows no redirects; uses a 5-second socket inactivity timeout, checks a 7-second response-body budget between and after 8 KiB reads, and caps responses at 256 KiB; records timeout, size, HTTP, and malformed-response failures explicitly.
runtime_dependencies: Task103 Crossref helper source in the same checkout

estimated_cost.basis: Crossref documents public REST access without signup. The wrapper permits at most ten serial requests, applies a 5-second socket timeout and a 7-second body-read budget with bounded chunks; no comparable latency, bandwidth, service-availability, or compute-cost profile has been measured.

alternatives.reason: The local validator checks the Evidence Program structure and recorded provenance but does not retrieve current Crossref metadata.

cards.fallback: If live network use is not approved or fails, retain the explicit NOT_RUN or acquisition failure and use a pinned historical Crossref source manifest only as historical evidence; never label it a live re-check.

negative_controls: Missing --allow-public-network makes no request and emits no result.
Reject URLs, malformed or duplicate DOI rows, duplicate JSON keys, and batches above ten before network access.
Only api.crossref.org is contacted; redirects, non-JSON, oversized responses, 404, timeout, and malformed JSON are explicit outcomes.
No repository files are written and network failures are not silently dropped.

router_conditions: Remain excluded unless the candidate ID is explicitly allowlisted and the typed route profile explicitly lists api.crossref.org in allowed_network_hosts.
A route proposal has execution_authorized=false and does not validate the caller authority behind that host list.
Every actual CLI invocation separately requires --allow-public-network and a task-specific decision to transmit the supplied DOI identifiers.
cards.claim_ceiling: Live Crossref bibliographic metadata retrieval and normalized title/year comparison only; response hashes bind received bytes, not source authenticity, article contents, scientific truth, or a complete retraction check.
